passages.p1: Read the email from Mark to his brother. Choose the correct word for each gap. The first one is done for you. Dear Tom, Yesterday I decided to [[1]] a big dinner for Mum's birthday. First, I needed to [[2]] all the vegetables. Then I [[3]] them into small pieces. I put the meat in the [[4]] for an hour. When it was ready, the food smelled really [[5]]. Everyone [[6]] the meal and said thank you.
passages.p2: Put the sentences in the correct order. The first sentence is fixed.
passages.p3:
A. For centuries, the world's highest mountain summits have captured the human imagination. Early explorers looked at these towering peaks with a mixture of fear and deep fascination, wondering what lay at the very top. Today, climbing to the highest points on Earth remains a lifelong dream for thousands of adventurers and outdoor enthusiasts. The motivation to conquer these massive geological formations often comes from a deep desire to test one's personal limits. Standing above the clouds offers a unique sense of achievement that few other experiences can match.

B. Escaping the comforts of sea level to climb high mountains takes a severe toll on the human body. As climbers ascend beyond 8,000 metres into what is known as the 'death zone', the amount of oxygen in the air drops remarkably. This lack of oxygen can lead to severe altitude sickness, causing extreme fatigue, intense headaches, and even life-threatening conditions. Climbers must spend weeks acclimatizing to the thinning atmosphere to give their bodies a chance to adjust. Even with proper preparation, the sheer physical exhaustion of moving upward through heavy snow and freezing winds is immense.

C. Beyond physical endurance, reaching a mountain summit requires an extraordinary amount of mental strength. Climbers often face isolation, unpredictable weather, and the constant, overwhelming fear of a fatal accident. In such hostile environments, a moment of panic or a small lapse in concentration can easily lead to disaster. It takes immense psychological resilience to keep putting one foot in front of the other when the body is screaming in pain. Successful alpinists are usually those who can maintain a calm, focused mindset despite the extreme stress of their surroundings.

D. In recent decades, the nature of summiting famous mountains has shifted significantly due to the growth of commercial expeditions. Peaks like Mount Everest, which were once exclusively reserved for professional alpinists, now attract hundreds of paying clients each season. Guiding companies provide fixed ropes, established camps, and carrying assistance, making the summits much more accessible to amateur climbers. However, this surge in popularity has led to dangerous overcrowding on narrow climbing routes. During brief periods of good weather, climbers can find themselves stuck in massive queues, significantly increasing the risks associated with exposure.

E. This influx of visitors has inevitably generated serious environmental consequences for these delicate high-altitude ecosystems. Decades of expeditions have left behind huge quantities of rubbish, including discarded oxygen bottles, torn tents, and plastic food wrappers. Furthermore, human waste has become a critical management issue, polluting the ice and threatening local water supplies in the valleys below. Several organizations and local governments have recently launched extensive clean-up campaigns to remove the accumulated debris. Despite these positive efforts, the fragile environments of the world's highest summits remain under intense pressure.

F. Modern technology has profoundly transformed the way people plan and execute high-altitude climbs today. Advances in materials science have led to the creation of ultra-lightweight clothing and equipment that offer ultimate protection against the freezing cold. Furthermore, satellite communications and highly accurate GPS devices ensure that climbers can easily contact rescue services in an emergency. Perhaps most surprisingly, highly detailed digital weather forecasting now allows expedition leaders to predict storms with incredible accuracy. These innovations have undoubtedly improved survival rates, though they can never entirely eliminate the natural dangers of the mountains.

G. Looking ahead, the global mountaineering community must find a delicate balance between encouraging exploration and preserving natural wonders. Strict regulations, such as limiting the number of climbing permits issued annually, are already being debated and implemented by authorities. Future climbers will need to adopt more sustainable and respectful practices to ensure the mountains remain pristine. Educational programs focusing on environmental responsibility are becoming a mandatory part of expedition training. Ultimately, the true triumph of reaching a summit will not just be about getting to the top, but doing so without leaving a permanent scar on the landscape.

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The meeting ended _____ — nobody expected it to finish so soon.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Chỗ trống bổ nghĩa cho động từ "ended" → cần trạng từ
2. Loại: sudden (adj) · suddenness (n) · {suddenly} (adv)
3. Đáp án: {suddenly} — trạng từ tả cách kết thúc
[/tuduy]
[td]Cuộc họp kết thúc đột ngột — không ai ngờ nó lại xong nhanh đến vậy.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The students listened _____ to the professor's lecture.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Chỗ trống bổ nghĩa cho động từ "listened" → cần trạng từ
2. Loại: careful (adj) · care (n) · {carefully} (adv)
3. Đáp án: {carefully} — trạng từ tả cách lắng nghe
[/tuduy]
[td]Các sinh viên chăm chú lắng nghe bài giảng của giáo sư.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

We cancelled the picnic because of the _____ wind.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Chỗ trống đứng trước danh từ "wind" → cần tính từ
2. Loại: strongly (adv) · strength (n) · {strong} (adj)
3. Đáp án: {strong} — tính từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ
[/tuduy]
[td]Chúng tôi hủy buổi dã ngoại vì gió mạnh.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Your idea sounds _____ to me. Let's try it.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "sounds" là linking verb (động từ nối) → cần tính từ mô tả chủ ngữ
2. Loại: {reasonable} (adj) · reasonably (adv) · reason (n)
3. Đáp án: {reasonable} — tính từ sau linking verb
[/tuduy]
[td]Ý tưởng của bạn nghe có vẻ hợp lý đấy. Hãy thử xem nào.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Don't shout — please speak more _____.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Chỗ trống bổ nghĩa cho động từ hành động "speak" → cần trạng từ
2. Loại: quiet (adj) · {quietly} (adv) · quietness (n)
3. Đáp án: {quietly} — trạng từ tả cách nói
[/tuduy]
[td]Đừng la lên — làm ơn nói nhỏ nhẹ hơn đi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

After ten years in Tokyo, Marcus speaks Japanese _____.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Chỗ trống bổ nghĩa cho động từ "speaks" → cần trạng từ
2. Loại: fluent (adj) · fluency (n) · {fluently} (adv)
3. Đáp án: {fluently} — trạng từ tả cách nói
[/tuduy]
[td]Sau mười năm ở Tokyo, Marcus nói tiếng Nhật trôi chảy.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The hotel room was _____, so we asked for a refund.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Sau "was" (linking verb) cần tính từ — nhưng chỗ trống là CỤM từ
2. Quy tắc: trạng từ + tính từ (adv bổ nghĩa adj): "terribly" bổ nghĩa cho "dirty"
3. Đáp án: {terribly dirty} — trạng từ + tính từ đúng thứ tự
[/tuduy]
[td]Phòng khách sạn bẩn kinh khủng, nên chúng tôi yêu cầu hoàn tiền.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The old bridge was _____ in the storm last night.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Câu bị động: "was _____" → cần trạng từ + phân từ quá khứ (V3)
2. "seriously" (adv) bổ nghĩa cho "damaged" (V3)
3. Đáp án: {seriously damaged} — trạng từ + quá khứ phân từ
[/tuduy]
[td]Cây cầu cũ bị hư hại nghiêm trọng trong trận bão tối qua.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The lift was broken yesterday, so we _____ the stairs to the tenth floor.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "yesterday" → quá khứ; diễn tả sự bắt buộc trong quá khứ
2. "must" không có dạng quá khứ → dùng "had to" thay thế
3. Đáp án: {had to climb} — bắt buộc ở quá khứ
[/tuduy]
[td]Hôm qua thang máy hỏng, nên chúng tôi phải leo cầu thang lên tầng mười.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I waited at the clinic for ages.' 'Oh really? How long _____ for the doctor?'
options: A. did you have to wait
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Câu hỏi về quá khứ → cần trợ động từ "did"
2. "have to" ở quá khứ: "did + S + have to + V"
3. Đáp án: {did you have to wait} — câu hỏi "have to" ở thì quá khứ
[/tuduy]
[td]"Mình chờ ở phòng khám lâu ơi là lâu." "Ồ thật à? Bạn phải chờ bác sĩ bao lâu?"[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Linda's new job is quite demanding. She _____ at six o'clock every morning.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Thì hiện tại, chủ ngữ "She" (ngôi 3 số ít) → chia động từ cho ngôi 3
2. "have to" → "has to" (ngôi 3 số ít)
3. Đáp án: {has to start} — bắt buộc ở hiện tại, ngôi 3
[/tuduy]
[td]Công việc mới của Linda khá vất vả. Cô ấy phải bắt đầu lúc sáu giờ mỗi sáng.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The car is making a strange noise again. I think we _____ it to the garage tomorrow.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "tomorrow" → tương lai; diễn tả sự bắt buộc sẽ xảy ra
2. "must" không có dạng tương lai → dùng "will have to"
3. Đáp án: {will have to take} — bắt buộc ở tương lai
[/tuduy]
[td]Xe lại phát ra tiếng lạ. Mình nghĩ ngày mai chúng ta sẽ phải mang nó ra ga-ra.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

(A friend recommends a film) 'That new documentary is brilliant. You _____ it — it's only on this week.'
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Đây là lời khuyên từ cảm nhận CÁ NHÂN của người nói
2. Lời khuyên mạnh (chủ quan) → "must"; quy định bên ngoài → "have to"
3. Đáp án: {must see} — nhấn mạnh lời khuyên cá nhân
[/tuduy]
[td]Bộ phim tài liệu mới đó tuyệt lắm. Bạn phải xem nó — chỉ chiếu tuần này thôi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

It's Saturday tomorrow, so I _____ get up early — I can have a lie-in for once.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Nghĩa: "không cần thiết" (không bắt buộc) ≠ "cấm"
2. "don't have to" = không cần; "mustn't" = cấm
3. Đáp án: {don't have to} — không bắt buộc phải dậy sớm
[/tuduy]
[td]Mai là thứ Bảy rồi, nên mình không cần dậy sớm — được ngủ nướng một bữa.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

This is a strict library. You _____ talk loudly or use your phone inside the reading room.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "strict library" + "inside the reading room" → quy định CẤM
2. "mustn't" = cấm; "don't have to" = không cần (nghĩa khác hoàn toàn)
3. Đáp án: {mustn't} — cấm đoán trong thư viện
[/tuduy]
[td]Đây là thư viện nghiêm khắc. Bạn không được nói to hay dùng điện thoại trong phòng đọc.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I can't come to the cinema tonight. I _____ finish this report before the morning.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Diễn tả sự bắt buộc ở hiện tại, dạng thân mật
2. "have got to" = dạng thân mật của "have to"; "must to" sai ngữ pháp (must + V nguyên)
3. Đáp án: {have got to} — bắt buộc hiện tại (thân mật)
[/tuduy]
[td]Tối nay mình không đi xem phim được. Mình phải làm xong báo cáo này trước sáng mai.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

My grandparents _____ in this village for over fifty years now.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "for over fifty years now" → khoảng thời gian kéo dài đến hiện tại
2. Hiện tại hoàn thành diễn tả hành động bắt đầu trong quá khứ, kéo dài đến nay
3. Đáp án: {have lived} — hiện tại hoàn thành với "for"
[/tuduy]
[td]Ông bà tôi đã sống ở ngôi làng này hơn năm mươi năm rồi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Look at those clouds! It _____ any minute.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "Look at those clouds" → có bằng chứng trước mắt để dự đoán
2. "be going to" dùng cho dự đoán dựa trên bằng chứng hiện tại
3. Đáp án: {is going to rain} — dự đoán có căn cứ
[/tuduy]
[td]Nhìn mấy đám mây kìa! Trời sắp mưa đến nơi rồi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Where have you been? I _____ for you for nearly an hour.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "for nearly an hour" → nhấn mạnh hành động kéo dài
2. Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn nhấn mạnh QUÁ TRÌNH + thời gian kéo dài
3. Đáp án: {have been waiting} — hoàn thành tiếp diễn nhấn mạnh quá trình
[/tuduy]
[td]Bạn đi đâu vậy? Mình đã đợi bạn gần một tiếng đồng hồ rồi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Sophie _____ her best friend Anna since they were children.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "know" là stative verb (động từ trạng thái) → không dùng dạng tiếp diễn
2. "since they were children" → hiện tại hoàn thành; "know" → "has known" (không "has been knowing")
3. Đáp án: {has known} — hoàn thành đơn với động từ trạng thái
[/tuduy]
[td]Sophie đã quen biết bạn thân Anna từ khi họ còn nhỏ.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

My uncle _____ in Berlin for the last six months — he works for a German bank there.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "for the last six months" → hành động kéo dài đến hiện tại
2. "live" là action verb → dùng được dạng tiếp diễn, nhấn mạnh tính tạm thời
3. Đáp án: {has been living} — hoàn thành tiếp diễn nhấn mạnh giai đoạn kéo dài
[/tuduy]
[td]Chú tôi đã sống ở Berlin suốt sáu tháng qua — chú làm cho một ngân hàng Đức ở đó.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I _____ Mr Wilson for ages. The last time I saw him was at the conference in 2018.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "for ages" + ngữ cảnh: khoảng thời gian từ quá khứ đến nay
2. Câu phủ định + "for ages" → hiện tại hoàn thành
3. Đáp án: {haven't met} — phủ định hiện tại hoàn thành
[/tuduy]
[td]Tôi đã không gặp ông Wilson lâu lắm rồi. Lần cuối tôi gặp ông là ở hội nghị năm 2018.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The cake _____ off the counter.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Quá khứ hoàn thành: "had" + V3 (phân từ quá khứ)
2. Phân từ của "fall": fall – fell – {fallen} (không phải "fell")
3. Đáp án: {had fallen} — đúng dạng V3 của "fall"
[/tuduy]
[td]Cái bánh đã rơi khỏi quầy bếp.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Lucy didn't want any soup. She _____ a huge sandwich an hour earlier.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "an hour earlier" → hành động xảy ra TRƯỚC một mốc quá khứ ("didn't want")
2. Hành động trước quá khứ → quá khứ hoàn thành
3. Đáp án: {had eaten} — quá khứ hoàn thành
[/tuduy]
[td]Lucy không muốn ăn súp. Cô ấy đã ăn một cái bánh sandwich to một tiếng trước đó.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I went to see the manager but he _____ the office.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "went" là quá khứ đơn → hành động rời văn phòng xảy ra TRƯỚC đó
2. Hành động trước quá khứ → quá khứ hoàn thành + "already"
3. Đáp án: {had already left} — quá khứ hoàn thành
[/tuduy]
[td]Tôi đến gặp quản lý nhưng ông ấy đã rời văn phòng rồi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

start
questions.explanation:
1. start (v) bắt đầu, khởi hành, khởi động
The game will start at three o'clock.(Trận đấu sẽ bắt đầu lúc ba giờ.)
2. begin (v) bắt đầu
The film is about to begin.(Bộ phim sắp sửa bắt đầu.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

finish
questions.explanation:
1. finish (v) hoàn thành; kết thúc
I need to finish my homework before dinner.(Tôi cần hoàn thành bài tập về nhà trước bữa tối.)
2. end (v) kết thúc
The film will end at nine o'clock.(Bộ phim sẽ kết thúc lúc chín giờ.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

fix
questions.explanation:
1. fix (v) sửa chữa
Can you fix my broken bike?(Bạn có thể sửa chiếc xe đạp hỏng của tôi không?)
2. repair (v) sửa chữa
The workers came to repair the old road.(Những người thợ đến sửa con đường cũ.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

close
questions.explanation:
1. close (v) đóng
Please close the door when you leave.(Làm ơn đóng cửa khi bạn rời đi.)
2. shut (v) đóng
She shut the window because of the cold.(Cô ấy đóng cửa sổ vì trời lạnh.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

big
questions.explanation:
1. big (adj) to; lớn
They live in a big house near the park.(Họ sống trong một ngôi nhà to gần công viên.)
2. large (adj) lớn; rộng
We ordered a large pizza for everyone.(Chúng tôi gọi một chiếc pizza lớn cho mọi người.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Something that you do
questions.explanation:
action (n) something that you do (hành động, việc làm)
The police took action to stop the crime. (Cảnh sát đã hành động để ngăn chặn tội phạm.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

An answer you give without being sure
questions.explanation:
guess (v) to give an answer without being sure (đoán, đưa câu trả lời khi chưa chắc chắn)
Can you guess the answer? (Bạn có đoán được câu trả lời không?)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Water that falls from the sky
questions.explanation:
rain (n) water that falls from the sky (mưa, nước rơi từ trời xuống)
We got caught in the rain. (Chúng tôi bị mắc mưa.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Caring about someone very much
questions.explanation:
love (v) to care about someone very much (yêu, yêu thương ai đó rất nhiều)
I love my family. (Tôi yêu gia đình mình.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

On the subject of someone or something
questions.explanation:
about (prep) on the subject of someone or something (về ai đó, về điều gì đó)
Tell me about your day. (Hãy kể cho tôi về ngày của bạn.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

do
questions.explanation: do homework = làm bài tập về nhà

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

heavy
questions.explanation: heavy rain = mưa to

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

bus
questions.explanation: bus stop = trạm xe buýt

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

take
questions.explanation: take a photo = chụp ảnh

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

fresh
questions.explanation: fresh air = không khí trong lành

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

You must make an ___ and study hard for your important exams this year.
questions.explanation: effort = nỗ lực

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

I really need some ___ about which computer to buy for my new job.
questions.explanation: advice = lời khuyên

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Would anyone like to make any ___ on the talk we just heard?
questions.explanation: comments = nhận xét

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

As my father grew ___, he gradually spent less and less time working at the office.
questions.explanation: older = già

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

I was trying to pay her a ___, but she completely misunderstood what I really meant.
questions.explanation: compliment = khen

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

While I was there, I wore a t-shirt and ___ almost every single day.
questions.explanation: jeans = quần bò

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

The Panorama is a rather ___ hotel in a back street near the city centre.
questions.explanation: run-down = cũ kỹ xuống cấp

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to your friend. Write about your feelings and what you think the club should do about the situation. Write about 50 words. Recommended time: 10 minutes.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Hi Sophie!
Did you hear the news? David Price isn't coming to our travel club meeting now, which is such a shame because I really wanted his autograph. We can still buy his book for twenty-five pounds, though. I think the club should ask him to send us some signed bookplates instead.
Talk soon,
Ben

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to the president of the club. Write about your feelings and what you think the club should do about the situation. Write 120–150 words. Recommended time: 20 minutes.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Dear President,
I am writing regarding the recent email about Mr David Price, who is no longer able to attend our next club meeting. I must admit that I felt quite disappointed by this news, as many of us had been looking forward to meeting him and having our books signed in person.
While I understand that such changes are sometimes unavoidable, I believe the club could do a little more for its members. It might be helpful if the committee asked Mr Price to provide signed bookplates that could be placed inside each copy. In addition, I would suggest arranging a short video message from him to be shown during the meeting.
I am confident that these small steps would help members feel valued.
Yours sincerely,
Daniel Carter

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Describe the picture?
questions.sampleAnswer: In this picture, a woman is sitting comfortably on a bus, looking out the window, perhaps lost in thought or enjoying the view. She's dressed casually, with her bag by her side. The bus interior is typical - seats arranged in rows, with some space around her. The soft light coming through the window highlights the peacefulness of the moment. Other passengers can be seen, but the focus is on her, suggesting a moment of quiet reflection during a daily commute or a short trip.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

When was the last time you went on vacation with someone else?
questions.sampleAnswer: The last time I went on vacation with someone else was about a year ago. I went with my close friends to the beach. It was a relaxing trip where we enjoyed swimming, sunbathing, and playing beach volleyball. We also visited some local restaurants and tried different types of food. It was a fun time because we were all able to relax and enjoy each other's company. I remember the experience clearly because it was simple but enjoyable.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

What are the benefits of hanging out with other people?
questions.sampleAnswer: Hanging out with others has a lot of benefits! It helps build strong social connections, which are important for emotional well-being. Spending time with friends or family can boost your mood, reduce stress, and provide support during tough times. It's also a great way to learn from others, try new things, and create fun memories. Being around people can even increase your sense of belonging and help you feel more connected to the world around you.

In the first picture, I see a woman. She is sitting on a sofa and using a laptop. She is buying things online. She looks happy.
In the second picture, I see a family in a shopping mall. They are walking and looking at clothes. They look very happy too.

questions.sampleAnswer: I think shopping online is very good. First, it is easy and fast. You can buy things at home. You don't need to go out. Second, things on the internet are often cheap. You can save money.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Which way of shopping do you prefer and why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I like shopping online more. Because I am busy, and it saves my time. I just use my phone to buy things. But sometimes, I go to the store to buy clothes because I want to try them on.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 4 - Discuss an abstract topic

Tell me a time when you were on your own.
questions.sampleAnswer: The last time I was alone was when I travelled to the forest. I wanted to see the trees and enjoy nature. I like being alone because it is very quiet, so I felt very relaxed and happy there. I love my friends, but sometimes I need to be alone because it is very good for me. When I am alone, I really like reading. I just sit and read a good book. I also like driving my car around my town. I listen to music and sing. I never sing with other people because I am shy.
